# PILOT-001 round-three council readiness review: **CHANGES_REQUESTED**

This covers design and harness readiness only. It is not validation of an implemented pilot and it does not approve construction. Reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh context, read-only, candidate `2c3db9d8`.

The one blocking defect is in `bundle.py`: it only checks the files Git tracks, so a source export with an extra file still builds, installs and reports `passed`. The fix is small and bounded. Everything else I reproduced passed, and my offline bundle run matched the round-3 receipt byte for byte.

## Mandatory findings

| ID | Severity | Location | Reproduction (in my own scratch) | Risk | Bounded fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OPUS-R3-01** | Medium | `harness/bundle.py:161-188` | I copied the clean baseline export and added `packages/friday-commands/src/friday_commands/injected_untracked.py`, then ran `bundle.py … --artifacts <raw125>`. It exited 0 with "Closed bundle passed". The extra file was inside the Commands wheel and sdist and in the installed neutral venv. `source_hashes` was identical to the clean run; only the wheel hash changed, and nothing compares that hash. | The check only covers files listed by `git ls-tree`. Any untracked or extra file in SOURCE goes into the workspace builds, yet the report certifies a "Git workspace build". This contradicts CD lines 332-333 ("verifies package build inputs … against the named Git revision"). Later G5 checks of sdist against Git cover only the changed Chat and Commands members; the other 11 workspace packages have no check. `capture.py` already refuses extra `src/` files, so the two tools disagree. | After the tracked-file loop, walk `packages/**` plus the root build files in SOURCE and refuse any file or symlink not in the tracked set. Alternatively, have `bundle.py` create its own `git archive` export. Add a negative control showing an extra file is refused. |
| **OPUS-R3-02** | Low | `harness/runner_wrapper.py:27-44` | Two runs through `pilot_run.py` with a writer command, both in my own lane: (a) a case-variant positional path `…/GUARD-SELFTEST.JSON` and (b) a short attached option `-o…/guard-selftest.log`. Both overwrote the earlier receipts (`CLOBBERED`). Exact, `--opt=`, and `/tmp`→`/private/tmp` alias paths were correctly refused. | CLD-R2-04 and the contract (lines 253-255) say every existing top-level JSON/log path is reserved. On the declared case-insensitive Darwin profile, the comparison is case-sensitive. The guard extension was given Darwin case folding but the wrapper was not. None of the documented commands trigger this. | On Darwin, compare case-folded resolved paths, as `guard_extension.py` already does. Also inspect the tail of short attached options (`-X<value>`). Add both as controls. |

**Advisory (not blocking):**
- **OPUS-R3-A1:** The bundle's child commands carry ambient uv state that the report doesn't record:
  - other `UV_*` variables are inherited, and no `--no-config` is passed;
  - `uv build` has no `--python`, so it picks an interpreter from `.python-version`, which says only `3.13`;
  - the report records neither the uv version nor `bundle.py`'s own hash.

  No drift happened here, because this machine has only one 3.13 installed (3.13.10).
- **OPUS-R3-A2:** The bundle's origin probe (line 462) skips modules that have no `__file__`, such as namespace packages.
- **OPUS-R3-A3:** ARGON-R2-ADV-002 is not fully closed. New current prose still contains run-together tokens: `through06` in `authority.json`, `has137` / `historical129` in the round-3 evidence limits, and `Python3.13.10` in the corrections map. Cosmetic only.

**CHANGES_REQUESTED — PILOT-001 design/harness readiness.**

**SOL-R3-PILOT-001 — High — Incomplete Git provenance permits untracked code into verified artifacts.**  
Location: [bundle.py:163](/Users/chuckrussell/Dev/gendev/agent-framework/docs/planning/active/command-refactor/validation/pilot/harness/bundle.py:163).

The source check validates expected Git blobs but never rejects additional build inputs, violating R-03/R-06’s complete provenance and clean-Git build requirements.

- **Reproduction:** In my own scratch Git export, added `packages/friday-commands/src/friday_commands/untracked_probe.py` containing `UNTRACKED_PROBE = True`, then ran the prescribed offline bundle command with the frozen baseline revision and provided raw artifacts.
- **Observed:** All 24 child commands exited zero; `bundle-report.json` reported `passed`. The Commands wheel contained `friday_commands/untracked_probe.py`, although that file was absent from Git and the report’s `source_hashes`. The capture harness correctly rejected this same export.
- **Risk:** Artifact hashes and successful isolated installs can certify a bundle containing code outside the declared revision.
- **Bounded mitigation:** Before builds, enforce exact build-input inventory equality with Git, including file types and symlinks, or construct a private verified export directly from Git. Add a negative control proving an extra package source/data file is rejected before building. Amend the diagnostic provenance claim accordingly; no product change is needed.
